links.reason: Line 2 முனம் ஆகிய பான்மை முளைத்து and line 4 மனமாம் நெறி give destiny and the heart together in 215, but 233 never mentions destiny, so the pair is the marker's contrast, not a qualification of one by the other. The 'minister' is only அறிவு in the packet's marking.
links.text_issue: gloss of 233's speaker rests on the marker

links.reason: Kuruntokai 251 has peacocks and pidavam fooled by a stray cloud's thunder (மாரி, முழங்குகுரல்); 1740 has the mullai fooled by an elephant's roar (அதிர்ந்துழிக் காரென் றெண்ணி). The conceit is shared, but nothing in the words shows the epic 'lifted' the poem, and the Kuruntokai verse nowhere says the friend means he has not broken his word.

248 weighs தோள்வலி against சூழ்ச்சி; 546 says not வேல் but கோல் that does not bend gives victory. Counsel and justice are not rival claims about the same thing, so there is no tension; the 'crooked counsel would fail' gain is the proposer's own addition.

Both put a serpent in the body-anthill (ஐம்பொறியாளன் உடம்பெனும் புற்று / போகமுட் புற்று). But the epic's snake is வேட்கை, desire, bitten by a look, not a five-senses serpent, and Tirumular's verse is flagged unclear; the 'taming' contrast and the yogic gain are not in the words.

211 asks pardon for the seizure (பிழையது பொறுக்க) and 57 narrates a seizure, so the pair is plausible. But 211 says seized with spider-thread like a lion, 57 says seized after his sword snapped in battle, and the Tamil does not fix them as one event.

The shared sea and raft (நோன்புணை / கடல் in 1132; காமக் கடல், ஏமப் புணை in 1164) are real, but the epic's sea is grief (கசிவெனுங் கடல்), not love, and the epic never answers or cites the couplet. Gains claiming a convention source and a supplied raft overstate it.

79 shows only one white hair seen in a mirror (ஒற்றை ... வெண்மை); the renunciation is not in the verse. Naladiyar 11 praises renouncing in infancy (குழவி யிடத்தே துறந்தார்) and does not call late renunciation wise, so the teaches is unsupported.

509 opens இடுக்கண்வந் துற்ற காலை ... நகுக and shares the idea of 621, but this is agreement, not development. The storm drowning all but Sitattan and composure failing to save the ship are not in the verse, which says laughter cuts trouble.

215 hymns the god as one who cut off Kama and was wrathful at Death (காமனைக் கடிந்தனை காலனைக் காய்ந்தனை); 1 praises the conqueror of வினையின் தொகை. Different conquests, so 215 does not 'name what he conquered' in 1; shared theme of a conquering god only.

1378 shows an army turn back when the crown falls (மணிமுடி ... வீழ்தலும்); Kural 770 says there is no army where leaders are absent. The king is not shown absent, only his crown fallen, so the epic illustrates rather than qualifies, and 'the army had no head' is not in the verse.

Kural 5 puts release in praising the Lord; 2815 says those who understand the two kinds of deed (இருசார் வினையும் தெளிந்தாரே) and the Lord's text neither exult nor scorn. The epic verse speaks of equal karmic fruit, not of deeds ceasing to cling, so a 'different account of how deeds stop clinging' is supplied by the note.
links.text_issue: verse is flagged repaired but readable

links.reason: 375 and Kural 6 share பொறி and a path that leads to good (நெறி). But 375 never reads or cites the couplet, so 'long life read as destruction of karma' belongs to the proposer. The pair is a shared theme, not a qualification.

Both use the moon's flaw (வெண்டிங்கள் ... விமலந்தனக் கில்லதன்றே; திங்கள் மறுவாற்றும்) to opposite ends: the poet claims the right to a fault, the noble cannot bear one. The pair is a sound image contrast, but qualifies does not fit; same_image does.

Both verses list the same ball tricks: மாலையுள் கரத்தலும் / அலங்கலுள் கரத்தலும், பை அரவின் ஆடலும் / ஈன்றரவி னாடலும், ஓட்டலும். The shared order and items show a stock catalogue, which the pair makes visible.

Siddhar 372 lists ஓமம், தர்ப்பணம், செபம், வேதம், ஆகமம் as pretence; it has no five-fires or grass-eating, and whether it condemns the rites or the performers is open. 1430's polemic needs 1435, outside this packet, to bear the 'keeps tapas' gain.

Pazhamozhi 15 links fine speech among the unlearned (கல்லாதவரிடைக் கட்டுரை) to a lapse of conduct (இழுக்கம்); Kural 719 forbids speaking well in a mean assembly. 'Develops' implies derivation the Tamil does not show; the ozhukkam grounding is a real addition.

360 argues from பல்லுயிர் in the body dying when it is given away; Kundalakesi 14 argues from புழுக்குலம் feeding on a deed-made body. Both use the teeming body, to opposite ends, but 14 is flagged unclear and its aim (denying 'mine') is not simply disgust.

1149 voices the shame of being rescued by a wife (தன்மனை யாளெனி னென்னையா வதிவ னாற்றலுங் கல்வியும்). Kural 903 is about stooping to a wife (இல்லாள்கண் தாழ்ந்த), not being rescued, so the 'cost on the woman' reading stretches the couplet and the gains are speculative.

The verse says he rants (அனன்றனன்) and will gather the people and then decide (பின்னைத் தக்கதொன் றறிவன்); he has not 'resolved'. Kural 568 faults a king who does not think with his circle and then rages, which is not this king, so the reversed-order claim misreads the verse.

1856 only asks whether conciliation, alliance, enmity or attack can overcome Death (காலன் றன்னை ... வெல்ல லாமோ); the failure of the devices is not in the verse. Naladiyar 6 (கூற்றம் குதித்துய்ந்தார் ஈங்கில்லை) answers the question in general, so the pair is a question and a rule, not a ruler's test shown failing.
1099 gives the bride with water before the fire and 1102 has him take her fingers and circle; this is rite sequence. Nothing in the Tamil says the gift 'only becomes a marriage' on the hand-taking.

1888's verse embraces Kanakamalai and the king's sons (சிறுவர் சேடார்) and rides out; it gives no motive, and 1817's friends promised to bring him to Vijayai. The 'not any call of his own' claim and 'with them' are not in the Tamil.

The pair connects only through Parimelazhagar's remarks, which this grading does not use. In the Kural words themselves 353 (ஐயத்தின் நீங்கித் தெளிந்தார்க்கு) says nothing of schools, and 242 (பல்லாற்றால் தேரினும் அஃதே துணை) does not speak of experience settling doubt.

The closing refrain is almost verbatim (எரிவளைத் / எரிவளர்த் திடுவதோ ரிளமை யெய்தினார்) and 84 adds திருவளர் செல்வர், but the 'shifts what women burn for' reading is thin and 84's line 2 is flagged unclear.

Both give the soul as distinct from the body (யாக்கை ... வேறாய் / இயல்பு வேறாம்). 238 does not show the pupil 'denying' it, and 50 shows no console or disproof, so the 'framed to meet doubt' teaching is the proposer's.

1599's அன்னளோ என்று நக்கான் suggests the claim is false, and 1581 shows a woman pleading with Civakan. But 1581 does not name Pavadattan's wife, so the contradiction needs the later verses, and 'household survives' is not in the Tamil.
links.text_issue: identification of 1581's speaker is not in the verse

links.reason: 138 narrates the killing (அண்ணல் வதை செய்தனன்) without comment; it does not say the story counts it as justice, so the 'absolute rule meets case' teaching claims more than the verse. Kural 321's rule is not tested by the verse.

Both place armies and elephants on a sea (இரண்டு கடல் எதிர்ந்த / மாக்கலம்; பௌவம் புணர் அம்பி). The sea of blood in the Kalavazhi is an aftermath, but the epic verse has no blood, so 'the aftermath its own image points to' and 'the moment before' are the proposer's.

269 says birth and death come from one's own deeds (தம் வினைப் பயத்தின் ஆகும்) and tells Vijayai grief is want of understanding; 308 has her say வினை செய்தேன் of her child's wretched birth. The doctrine meant to console becomes the ground of her self-blame, a limit on the consolation.

2868 says killing brings great suffering (உயிர்க் கொலையும் வேண்டா); Kural 321 already states both rule and result (கோறல் பிறவினை எல்லாந் தரும்), so the Kural does not lack a reason. The swans and prince scene is not in the verse.
Both verses set the adorned body (சாந்து, கோதை) against its ruin, but the epic has no vultures or cart axle, and draws no lesson. A shared theme of the ruined beloved body, not a qualification.

908 has Suramanjari vow none shall break her இறை/நிறை but Civakan, and 2061 has him say her hair-line took his திண்ணிறை. The echo of நிறை is real, but this is a reversal or fulfilment, not an incompatible claim, and 'breaks first on his side' is the proposer's gloss.

446's priest foretells a youth coming blazing in anger (உடன்றெரி துளும்ப); 681 has anger kindled at the word 'tribute'. Neither verse names Tivittan or the foe, and both are flagged uncertain, so the fulfilment is read from the larger plot.

2822 defines சீலம் as பழித்தன வொழித்தல், and Kural 280 says பழித்தது ஒழித்து விடின், so they agree. The plucked-hair discipline of 2820 is outside the verse, and the couplet gains no mark-bearing case from 2822.

1315 says her sickness is தன் கண் தரு காமநோய்; Kural 1171 has eyes showing him and bringing the sickness. The eyes as cause is shared, but the epic merely states it, not blames the eyes, and 'first night' is not in the verse.

2107 compares the pace of crossing a desert to the fame-seeker's wealth leaving (நிதியமே போன்று); that he gives it away is the marker's uncertain reading. The pair shares புகழ் and standing in an unstable world, but a 'transaction' teaching is not shown by the words.

53 says only Kama's arrows mingled (காமவேள் கவர்கணை) in the king's days; 466 has women going to report to Kama their victory over lovers (காமுகர் படை ... வென்றி). The shared Kama war is a theme; the women in 466 are different people in another setting, and 466 is flagged.

229 asks which youth is fit; 238 sends for ministers learned in policy (நீதி மாக்களை). That follows the question in plot order but does not answer it, and 'marriage a matter of counsel' is a general gloss.

Both praise the Jina as the one who broke fierce deeds (வெவ்வினை நூறி / வெங்கண் வினை போழ்ந்து). The repeated claim is a shared formula; the 'matches the epic's account' teaching is only the shared theme.

58 shows a man led to the goddess's sacrifice with the king's sword drawn; Kural 259 weighs ghee oblations (அவிசொரிந்து) against not killing. Different rites, and the king is not weighing anything in 58, so the 'weigher' gain is false.
2913 decrees the boy (பெருநம்பி யாக) and 2914 crowns him; this is plot sequence. The giver and crowner are not named in 2914 (flagged), so 'the whole court's weight' is the proposer's.

49 names the child சீர்பிரதா பந்தன்; 53 has the king rename him நாகநற் குமரன் because the serpent held him (நாகத்தின் சிரசின் மீது ... தரித்தென்று). The second name replaces the first by the king's own act, as the note says.

Kural 1071 says the base look like men (மக்களே போல்வர்); 1975 says they are human only by birth (மக்கட் பிறப்பெனு மாத்திர) and otherwise animals, without shame or conduct. The idea is shared, but the Kural verse does not set a conduct test and 1975 does not tie the test to birth, so the teaches and gains are muddled.
